subject: Annual planning: target bands, scenario gates & owner onboarding

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightSky Advisors <anna@brightsky.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Annual planning: target bands, scenario gates & owner onboarding

Team —

Kicking off the FY27 planning thread for targets and scenario bands. Goal is to agree on three clear funding scenarios (A / B / C), define gating thresholds, and assign owners for the scenario runbook so we can finish QBR-ready decks by the week of July 13. Key asks below.

Attachments: FY27_Scenario_Bands_v2.xlsx, QBR_prep_checklist.pdf (stubs attached)

Quick context: finance modeled three outcome bands in the attachment — baseline (A), conservative (B), and contingency (C). Each band has implied hiring, R&D spend, and dedicated capacity commits. We surfaced two sensitive levers: batch/quantization policy impact on inference cost and committed Dedicated capacity for sales-assist customers.

Please action the following by EOD Friday, June 18: 
- Owners: confirm who is the accountable owner for each scenario row (cost, revenue assumption, headcount). I propose: Vivek (Product model roadmap owner, model-cost deltas), Marissa (revenue/GT M assumptions), Rishi (engineering headcount & infra cost), Laura (talent/hiring cadence). Reply with "ACK + owner name".
- Redlines: flag any assumptions in the spreadsheet that are non-negotiable for your area. Add comments directly in the sheet (drive link below).
- QBR checklist: skim the attached and add missing deliverables.

I'll hold a short 30-min alignment on Thursday (06/17) 10:00–10:30 PT to lock owners and timeline. Invite pending.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Finance
Redwood Inference

Neha —

ACK. I can take lead on the product/model cost deltas and own the model-specific assumptions (sequence length distributions, expected throughput improvements from our runtime, quantization profiles). I reviewed FY27_Scenario_Bands_v2 and added inline comments where we need more granularity on per-model latency/cost impact.

Two small asks:
- Move the canary signoff date for scenario B to June 25 (gives us time to run the A/B inference runs on dedicated clusters).
- Add a short row for model-tier fallback cost (what we expect if we shift traffic to a cheaper LLM variant).

I'll slot someone from the runtime team into Thursday's 10:00 sync.

—Vivek

Neha / all —

Quick notes from a people/hiring lens:
- I support the owner assignments Vivek proposed. For headcount, we need a stronger bridge between hiring cadence and offer lead times — if scenario A assumes 40 hires in R&D, we cannot compress interviews into July; recruiting runway is 8–10 weeks for senior ICs. Please add a separate column for "recruiting lead time" and an ask to prioritize roles that unblock revenue.
- Scenario C should include an explicit hiring freeze step and a template redeploy plan for engineers and product managers; otherwise we underestimate cost of context switching.
- I uploaded a short CSV with high-risk roles to owner_rundown_smallsheet.csv — flagged roles where backfill is hard (model infra, infra security).

If it's helpful, I can join Thursday's sync and run through the recruiting timelines live.

Thanks,
Laura
Head of People & Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks — added a short economics sanity check. Two requests:
1) Can we define a specific metric set to declare when to transition between bands? I propose: 90-day gross margin delta > 4% (for downgrades), ARR acceleration (3-mo rolling) < 2% for two consecutive months triggers conservative scenario, and burn runway under 9 months triggers contingency C.
2) I'll run a 6-month sensitivity sim against our baseline (assumes the product roadmap delivers X). Can someone assign the raw model-cost deltas to me (Vivek/Rishi)?

Also cc'ing BrightSky (Anna) who can run an independent sensitivity for ARR assumptions.

—Jonas
Head of Strategy
Redwood Inference

Neha —

ACK + Rishi for engineering headcount and infra cost. Quick updates from infra:
- We can provide the per-token cost delta estimates by June 22 if Vivek's team shares model-size and expected throughput assumptions (batch sizes, p50/p95 latencies).
- For scenario C (contingency), we recommend an implementation plan that includes automated prefix/KV cache eviction policies and a staged quantization fallback (8-bit first, 4-bit as last resort). This needs a short runbook and a QA window — suggest we reserve a 2-week QA slot in July.

I added a comment on the spreadsheet re: dedicated capacity churn assumptions.

—Rishi

Thanks all — good alignment. Summary and next steps: 

Decisions made:
- Owners: Vivek (model cost deltas), Marissa (revenue & GTM assumptions), Rishi (engineering cost & QA for fallback), Laura (hiring cadence & recruiting lead time).
- Metrics that trigger band transitions: as Jonas proposed (90-day gross margin delta >4%; ARR accel <2% for 2 months; runway <9 months).
- Gates: Canary signoff for scenario B moved to June 25. QA window for contingency quantization fallback reserved July 6–20.

Action list (owners + deadlines):
- Vivek: deliver model-size and throughput assumptions (sheet row updates) by June 20.
- Rishi: per-token cost delta estimates by June 22 and draft fallback runbook by June 30.
- Laura: populate recruiting lead times and flagged roles in the spreadsheet by June 21.
- Marissa: confirm revenue assumptions and plug ARR sensitivity into the sheet by June 22.
- Neha: assemble QBR-ready slide skeleton and circulate on July 6.

Please ACK these items in-line in the sheet and copy me on any major redlines. If you need an slot change for the 06/17 sync, tell me now — otherwise I'll send the Calendar invite.

Attachments referenced: FY27_Scenario_Bands_v2.xlsx, QBR_prep_checklist.pdf, owner_rundown_smallsheet.csv

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Finance
Redwood Inference
